meta.title: Independent Drata Administrator Competency Proposal
meta.summary: An unapproved portfolio draft for the Drata Administrator role with 5 domains, 20 tasks, and 60 KSAs.
meta.disclosure: Independent portfolio proposal by Justin Oh. Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or reviewed by Drata. Product administration is not compliance assurance.
meta.footer: Independent portfolio work. Simulated reviews are not human approvals; structural checks are not semantic validation.

pipelineStages.title: Role intake
pipelineStages.summary: Normalized the exact target role for the draft pipeline.

pipelineStages.title: Research planning
pipelineStages.summary: Planned collection from current official product documentation.

pipelineStages.title: Evidence collection
pipelineStages.summary: Retained only exact, source-specific excerpts after quarantining the failed legacy transport.

pipelineStages.title: Evidence synthesis
pipelineStages.summary: Reduced the collected material to the source set used by the draft analysis.

pipelineStages.title: Initial job-task draft

pipelineStages.title: Domain analysis
pipelineStages.summary: Organized the proposed work into domains and task statements.

pipelineStages.summary: Mapped draft knowledge, skill, and ability statements to the proposed domains.

pipelineStages.title: Challenge review
pipelineStages.summary: Challenged evidence coverage, role distinctiveness, and unsupported numeric precision.

pipelineStages.title: SME perspective panel

domains.name: User, Role & Access Administration
domains.rationale: Proposed User, Role & Access Administration domain. Its 25% weight remains unvalidated pending practitioner evidence.

tasks.statement: Assign, change, or remove the Admin role for platform users to control top-level system permissions
Read the RBAC access matrix to decide the correct role for each workspace user

Identify and avoid risky or conflicting role combinations to preserve separation of duties; where true separation of duties is not structurally possible (e.g., a solo-admin organization), apply and document compensating controls instead
Grant or restrict remote access permission for Drata Support sessions
Confirm workspace access scope remains correct after modifying a user's role assignment

domains.name: Organizational Governance & Key Personnel Management
domains.rationale: Proposed Organizational Governance & Key Personnel Management domain. Its 15% weight remains unvalidated pending practitioner evidence.

tasks.statement: Keep Key Personnel records (Executive Team, Security Committee, Board of Directors) accurate and assigned to active personnel

Configure remaining Admin-exclusive organization settings — org-wide language, notification and ticket-automation rules, API keys, and Quick Start — consolidated into one task because the only evidence is an enumerative list of page names with no per-setting procedural detail; actual frequency likely varies by organization
Manage workspace details: name, icon, URL, description, and assigned managers

domains.name: System Integrations & Connections Management
domains.rationale: Proposed System Integrations & Connections Management domain. Its 30% weight remains unvalidated pending practitioner evidence.

tasks.statement: Set up third-party system connections using dedicated service accounts with least-privilege, read-only access

Connect systems in the vendor-recommended order — identity provider, then infrastructure, then version control, then ticketing — noting that real-world sequencing may instead follow procurement timelines rather than this textbook order
Check connection health status and review AI-generated summaries that explain failed syncs (Connection Insights)
Troubleshoot and fix unhealthy connections to keep automated evidence collection running continuously

domains.name: Compliance Framework, Controls & Evidence Management
domains.rationale: Proposed Compliance Framework, Controls & Evidence Management domain. Its 22% weight remains unvalidated pending practitioner evidence.

tasks.statement: Map manual, file-based, or URL-based evidence to controls to show the controls are ready
Map or unmap policies to controls — including reviewing auto-mapped template policies — to keep traceability accurate
Mark framework requirements in or out of scope and record the business reason for the decision
Check how a scope change affects control readiness and the framework's overall readiness percentage

Assign and maintain multiple compliance frameworks (e.g., SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, GDPR) on a workspace, including ongoing scope adjustments as frameworks are added over time — distinct from task-2-3's one-time workspace setup

domains.name: Access Reviews & Personnel Data Management
domains.rationale: Proposed Access Reviews & Personnel Data Management domain. Its 8% weight remains unvalidated pending practitioner evidence.

tasks.statement: Upload or update personnel access data by CSV for manually added (non-connected) applications during access reviews
Tell apart connected applications (access data syncs automatically) from manually added applications (CSV upload required) when preparing access reviews
Use the provided CSV template so all required fields are complete before uploading access review data

items.statement: Knowledge of what the Admin role permission grants at the platform/system level in Drata.
Skill in assigning, changing, or removing a platform user's Admin role through Drata's user management interface.
Ability to judge whether granting, changing, or revoking a user's Admin role is appropriate given the requester's job function and organizational risk.
Knowledge of the structure and contents of the RBAC access matrix, including the permission scope of each defined role.
Skill in reading the RBAC access matrix to select the correct role for a given workspace user's job function.
Knowledge of role combinations that create separation-of-duties conflicts and of compensating-control concepts for organizations where true separation of duties is not structurally possible.
Ability to evaluate a proposed role assignment for separation-of-duties conflicts.
Skill in configuring role-based or custom permission boundaries so that conflicting duties (e.g., implementing a control and approving its own evidence) are not held by the same user.
Knowledge of the need for periodic review of role assignments to detect separation-of-duties conflicts introduced after initial setup.
Ability to design and document a compensating control when true separation of duties is not structurally achievable for a given role combination.
Knowledge of the permission controlling Drata Support's remote access to a workspace and its security implications.
Skill in granting or restricting the remote-access permission for Drata Support sessions.
Knowledge of how a role change propagates to a user's workspace access scope.
Ability to verify that a user's workspace access scope is correct and intended after modifying their role assignment.
Knowledge of the Key Personnel categories required for governance records (Executive Team, Security Committee, Board of Directors).
Skill in updating Key Personnel records to keep assignments current with active personnel.
Ability to judge when a personnel change (e.g., departure, role change) requires a Key Personnel record update to remain audit-accurate.
Knowledge of how Key Personnel records serve as evidentiary support for governance and oversight requirements across compliance frameworks.
Knowledge of the Admin-exclusive organization settings pages (notifications, ticket-automation rules, API keys, Quick Start).
Knowledge of org-wide language/localization settings and their relevance to multinational organizations.
Knowledge of API key management concepts, including scope and rotation considerations, within organization settings.
Skill in configuring notification and ticket-automation rules at the organization level.
Skill in generating and managing API keys and completing Quick Start configuration tasks.
Knowledge of the workspace detail fields (name, icon, URL, description, assigned managers) and their purpose.
Knowledge of how workspace identity fields (name, URL, description) support distinguishing between multiple workspaces within a multi-entity organization.
Skill in editing workspace details and assigning workspace managers.
Ability to determine appropriate workspace manager assignments based on organizational accountability structure.
Knowledge of least-privilege, read-only service-account design principles for third-party system connections.
Skill in setting up a third-party system connection using a dedicated, least-privilege service account.
Ability to assess whether a proposed connection's access scope meets least-privilege requirements before activating it.
Skill in documenting a connection's service-account credentials and granted access scope to support an audit trail at setup time.
Knowledge of the vendor-recommended connection order (identity provider, infrastructure, version control, ticketing) and awareness that real-world sequencing may follow procurement timelines instead.
Knowledge of dependencies between connection types, such as an identity provider connection enabling personnel and device correlation for later integrations.
Skill in sequencing multiple system connections to align with both platform recommendations and organizational procurement constraints.
Ability to prioritize connection setup order when vendor procurement timelines conflict with the platform-recommended sequence.
Knowledge of connection health status indicators and the purpose of AI-generated Connection Insights summaries.
Skill in checking connection health status and interpreting Connection Insights summaries to identify failed syncs.
Ability to analyze a Connection Insights summary to determine the root cause of a failed sync.
Skill in troubleshooting and remediating an unhealthy connection to restore automated evidence collection.
Ability to diagnose recurring connection failures and implement a fix that keeps automated evidence collection running continuously.
Knowledge of evidence types (manual, file-based, URL-based) and how each maps to control readiness requirements.
Skill in mapping manual, file-based, or URL-based evidence to the correct controls.
Knowledge of the policy-to-control mapping model, including auto-mapped template policies.
Skill in mapping or unmapping policies to controls and reviewing auto-mapped template policies for accuracy.
Knowledge of the criteria and documentation requirements for marking a framework requirement in or out of scope.
Skill in marking framework requirements in or out of scope within Drata.
Ability to evaluate and document a defensible business justification for a scope decision on a framework requirement.
Knowledge of how scope changes propagate to control readiness and overall framework readiness percentage.
Ability to analyze the downstream effect of a scope change on control and framework readiness.
Knowledge of the compliance frameworks supported for workspace assignment (e.g., SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, GDPR) and ongoing scope-maintenance requirements.
Skill in assigning and maintaining multiple compliance frameworks on a workspace, including ongoing scope adjustments as frameworks are added.
Skill in configuring shared control mappings across multiple frameworks to avoid duplicating evidence collection effort.
Ability to evaluate the impact of adding a new compliance framework on existing control scope and overall readiness across the workspace.
Knowledge of when a CSV upload is required to provide personnel access data for manually added applications during access reviews.
Skill in uploading or updating personnel access data via CSV for manually added applications.
Skill in using the provided CSV template to ensure all required fields are complete before uploading access review data.
Knowledge of the required fields and format validation enforced by the CSV template for manually added application access data.
Knowledge of the distinction between connected applications (automatic access-data sync) and manually added applications (CSV upload required).
Ability to correctly classify an application as connected or manually added when preparing an access review.
Skill in reconciling discrepancies between uploaded CSV access data and known personnel records during an access review.

reviews.label: Not human approved
reviews.title: Evidence challenge
reviews.summary: weak. All retained evidence comes from one vendor-owned Help Center domain; no labor-market, practitioner, or independent framework corroboration exists. Domain 5 remains thin: three task statements rest on one short article and the source does not establish Administrator-exclusive ownership. Several organization-setting tasks are inferred from a page-name list without procedural evidence. Numeric weights, frequencies, and criticality values remain hypotheses despite their precise representation. Shared-role work is a large part of the proposed Administrator scope, reducing role distinctiveness.

reviews.label: Not human approved
reviews.title: Simulated SME perspectives
reviews.summary: no-valid-human-consensus. Every persona was explicitly fictional and simulated; none supplied practitioner evidence or approval. The simulated perspectives disagreed on domain weights and task cadence across enterprise, small-organization, assessment, and international contexts. Repeated concerns were the single-source evidence base and weak support for Domain 5. Suggestions about compensating controls, procurement ordering, audit-log review, localization, and data residency were not source evidence.

reviews.label: Not human approved
reviews.title: Bias and fairness review
reviews.summary: pass-with-notes-model-label-only. Precise numeric judgments create credential-inflation risk when evidence confidence is low. Dense task language may add construct-irrelevant reading load for non-native English speakers and candidates with reading disabilities. Hands-on tasks assume employer-sponsored access to a configured Drata tenant; no alternative sandbox was established. Future assessment content must be screen-reader compatible and must not depend solely on visual matrices or dashboards. The reported readability score was a model estimate, not a measured result.

reviews.label: Not human approved
reviews.title: Independent publication QA
reviews.summary: publication-blocked. The exact role is Drata Administrator, but page access does not by itself prove day-to-day role ownership or task frequency. All public source excerpts are exact substrings of the named, hash-bound official receipt body. The structural verification does not bind each complete task or KSA claim to a semantically supporting excerpt. Compensating-control, procurement-timeline, periodic-review, API-rotation, shared-control-mapping, and discrepancy-reconciliation details need dedicated support before publication. The artifact named FinalJTA is a reconciled model draft, not a human-finalized JTA.

validationNext: Run a real practitioner panel for the exact Drata Administrator role and retain named review records, conflicts, and approvals.
Bind every complete task and KSA claim to an exact source excerpt and receipt hash, then perform independent semantic-support review rather than URL-membership checking.
Validate domain weights, task frequency, and criticality using practitioner survey or observed-work evidence; do not treat current numbers as estimates with known precision.
Collect independent corroboration beyond vendor documentation, including role postings or practitioner evidence, and document disagreements with the vendor-defined capability model.

Remove or separately source the known unsupported extensions covering compensating controls, procurement timing, periodic reviews, API-key rotation, shared-control mappings, and CSV discrepancy reconciliation.

Observe representative tasks in a current authorized tenant and distinguish Admin-exclusive duties from capabilities shared with Workspace Manager, Information Security Lead, Control Manager, DevOps Engineer, or Access Reviewer roles.
Complete human plain-language, accessibility, internationalization, and role-access review, including a fair practice path for people without employer-sponsored tenant access.
Treat exam blueprinting, item writing, standard setting, piloting, psychometrics, and cut-score decisions as later gated work; none was completed or approved in this run.
